title: An easy and fast way to obtain a high number of glial cells from rat cerebral tissue: A beginners approach.
protocol: Dissect the brains of P0-P2 neonatal rat pups using sterile large scissors and place heads into a petri dish with 70% ethanol.
Transfer the head to a petri dish containing cold DMEM.
Hold the nose portion of the head with Mouse-teeth forceps and cut the skin and skull from the nose to the foramen magnum using curved forceps.
Expose the whole brain and remove nervous tissue from the skull base while keeping olfactory bulbs intact.
Place the head in a new petri dish containing cold DMEM.
Under a dissecting magnifying glass, use thin Dumont forceps to remove the meningeal layer following instructions in Supplementary video 1 online.
Remove the meningeal layer from the inner midbrain and cut between hemispheres to eliminate them.
Clamp the olfactory bulbs and remove the meningeal layer from both hemispheres.
Carefully open the hemispheres, remove the chorioideal plexus covering of the inside, and remove brainstem and cerebellum.
Place all forebrains in new petri dishes containing cold DMEM.
Transfer forebrains to a 50ml Falcon tube using Dumont forceps.
Add approximately 0.5 ml of DMEM media to the tube.
Gently triturate and dissociate nervous tissue with a serum-coated Pasteur pipette, adding small amounts of DMEM as needed until a homogenate is formed in the media.
Centrifuge the tubes for 10 minutes at 168g (~1000 r.p.m.).
Discard the supernatant by aspiration carefully.
Suspend the pellet in 20 ml of warm DMEM (10:10:1 per forebrain).
Seed Poly-D-Lysine covered 75 cm² flasks with 10 ml of cell suspension each.
Incubate at 37°C in a water-saturated 5% CO₂ atmosphere for 7 to 10 days without changing the culture medium.
Close the flasks properly after incubation time.
Place the flasks on an orbital shaker and shake at 230 r.p.m. for 3 hours.
Centrifuge the cell suspension for 10 min at 168g.
Add warm DMEM 10:10:1 to the flasks and place them in the orbital shaker immediately after centrifugation if proceeding with OPCs/astrocytes isolation.
Discard the supernatant by aspiration carefully.
Suspend the pellet in 1ml of warm DMEM 10:10:1.
Gently mix 10 μl of homogenate with 80 μl of PBS and 10 μl of Trypan Blue to determine viable cell count.
Count the number of non-stained microglial cells using a Neubauer chamber.
Calculate the total number of viable cells by dividing the counted cells by 4, then multiplying by 105.
Dilute the cell suspension with warm DMEM 10:10:1 to the desired concentration.
Incubate for 24 hours in a tissue culture incubator at 37°C with 5% CO2.
Use Poly-D-lysine coated plates for in vitro experiments involving microglial cells.
Ensure that flasks are completely closed before shaking in a low O2 environment.
Filter cell suspension through a sterile 30 μm nylon mesh.
Add warm DMEM 10:10:1 to the flasks if proceeding with astrocyte isolation.
Transfer filtered cell suspension to untreated Petri dishes and incubate for 1-1.5 hours.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 168g for 10 minutes.
Discard supernatant by aspiration, taking care not to aspirate the loose pellet.
Suspend the pellet in 1 ml of warm DMEM 10:10:1.
Determine the number of viable cells.
Dilute the cell suspension to a maximum concentration of 100,000 viable cells/ml with warm DMEM 10:10:1.
Plate and incubate for 3h in a tissue culture incubator with 5% CO2 at 37°C.
Replace the culture media of the flasks with 5 ml of warm PBS each.
Wash twice while gently shaking the flasks in the laminar flow hood.
Remove the PBS and add 5ml of Trypsin (0.05%) - EDTA (0.02%).
Place the flasks in the incubator for 5-10 minutes and gently shake them to raise the cells from the bottom.
Add 5 ml of DMEM 5:5:1 each to inactivate the enzyme, gently mix and collect all supernatants.
Pellet by centrifugation for 10 min at 168g.
Discard the supernatant by aspiration carefully.
Suspend the pellet in 1 ml of warm DMEM 5:5:1.
Determine the number of viable cells.
Dilute the cell suspension to the desired number of cells with warm DMEM 5:5:1.
Plate and incubate for 24 hours in a tissue culture incubator at 37°C with 5% CO2.
